title: MiniMax M3 ships weights but trails its SWE-Bench Pro claim on rerun by Q3 2026
body: By Q3 2026 MiniMax publishes the M3 checkpoint and technical report on Hugging Face and GitHub, making the open-weight commitment a fact rather than a press claim and letting outside engineers self-host the 1M-context model and its Sparse Attention design. But when independent evaluators run M3 on SWE-Bench Pro under a public harness, the verified figure lands materially below the company-reported 59.0% headline, so the model no longer cleanly sits ahead of GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro on a reproducible measurement. The gap follows from the launch shape itself: at announcement the 59.0% and the 83.5 BrowseComp numbers came from MiniMax's own infrastructure with no external scaffold or scoring details disclosed, and agentic-coding scores are notoriously sensitive to harness, tool access, retry budget, and prompt construction. The business consequence is that the weights ship as promised yet the parity story softens, hardening a hosted-API-first, weights-and-report-later pattern in which the launch-day leaderboard claim and the later reproducible result are treated as two separate events by buyers.

reasoning.because: M3 launched API-only June 1 on self-reported 59.0% SWE-Bench Pro; weights only promised in ~10 days
reasoning.given: Open-weight launches increasingly lead with hosted APIs and self-reported, unreproduced scores
reasoning.so_that: M3 weights land on Hugging Face but independent SWE-Bench Pro reruns post a materially lower figure than 59.0%
reasoning.landing: by Q3 2026; checkpoint on MiniMaxAI HF org + 1 third-party eval below the claim
reasoning.plain_language: MiniMax says its new coder beats GPT-5.5, but until others test the real weights, expect the public score to come in lower.

summary: MiniMax bills M3 as open-weight and posts a 59.0% SWE-Bench Pro score on its own hardware, but the checkpoint is not out yet. Expect the weights to ship on Hugging Face this quarter while independent reruns land below that figure, separating the open-weight claim from a reproducible result.
